plan: Store a defensive copy of the appointments (id/label only) and the optional action source and screen sink in the constructor; initialize the public `session` dict from a single `_initial_session` factory so begin and abandon reuse it.
Route `handle` through a dispatch table from action type to a per-action handler method, with up-front guards for non-dict actions and unknown types returning error screens instead of raising.

Build every screen through one `_screen(prompt, messages)` factory that emits exactly the keys `prompt`, `messages`, `choices`, and populates choices (in appointment input order) exactly when the prompt is `Choose appointment`.

Have each handler validate preconditions (active/incomplete session via a shared `_require_active_incomplete` guard, payload type checks, known-id membership against a list to avoid hashing errors) and return an `Error:`-prefixed screen before any mutation, so rejected actions never corrupt accepted data.
Compute post-correction prompts with a `_next_prompt` helper that returns the first unmet step: `Confirm contact`, then `Choose appointment`, then `Review and complete`.

Implement `run_once` to raise `RuntimeError` when either collaborator is missing before invoking either, then perform read_action -> handle -> display exactly once and return the displayed screen object.
mechanisms: Dispatch table mapping action `type` strings to handler methods
Single `_screen` factory enforcing the frozen screen dictionary shape and the choices-only-on-`Choose appointment` rule
Validate-then-mutate handler structure with a shared active/incomplete precondition guard
`_initial_session` factory shared by construction, `begin`, and `abandon` for clean resets
List-based known-id membership check that tolerates unhashable payload values without raising
Constructor-injected `action_source`/`screen_sink` duck-typed collaborators with a missing-collaborator `RuntimeError` in `run_once`
